# Sensitivity analysis for bias in multiple imputation {#sec-appC}

In this analysis, for the conditions when multiple imputation produced the highest bias, i.e. when $ICC = 0.1$ and $\gamma_{01} = .4$, alternative inverse Wishart priors were specified for the level-2 covariance matrix based on the true parameter values:  

$$
\tau_{\text{guess}} =
\begin{bmatrix}
.1 & 0   & 0 \\
0   & .1 & 0 \\
0   & 0   & 1
\end{bmatrix}
$$

This corresponds to the two standardized Level-1 variables $Y$ and $X$ and the Level-2 variable $\bar{X}$.

The covariance prior was defined as

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau} \sim \mathcal{IW}(\nu, \mathbf{S}),
\qquad
\mathbf{S} = 3\,\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\text{guess}}
$$
Summarized results of this analysis can be found in @tbl-jomo.

```{r, results='asis', echo=FALSE, message=FALSE}
#| label: tbl-jomo
#| tbl-cap: "Bias reduction with alternative priors"
library(here)
jomotable <- read.table(here("results", "jomotable.csv"))
library(kableExtra)
library(dplyr)
jomotable %>%
  select(-beta) %>%
  kable(
    format = "latex",
    escape = TRUE,
    booktabs = TRUE,
    align = "c",
    col.names = c("N2", "Bias ui", "rel. Bias ui", "Bias wi", "rel. Bias wi", "Bias red.")
  ) %>%
  pack_rows(index = c("MCAR" = 3, "MAR" = 3)) %>%
  column_spec(1:6, width = "1.8cm") %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, 
                position = "center", 
                latex_options = "hold_position") %>%
  landscape() %>%
  row_spec(0, bold=TRUE) %>%
  footnote(
    general = "Fußnote zur Erklärung TEst",
    threeparttable = TRUE
  ) %>%
  print()

```
